clue.text: Out of water, over-excited fellow has the doctor in

parts.note: someone over-excited is high, as on drugs or adrenaline

indicators.note: in says the doctor's letters go inside the fellow's name

parts.note: Andy is a man's name, so any fellow will do
Dr is the standard abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: An agitated man has called the doctor round to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has ... in' reads like inviting a doctor round; 'in' puts the doctor's letters inside the fellow's name, after its D.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat left stranded by the tide sits beached, which is the idiom's literal origin.

clue.text: Drink pop

definitions.meaning: a white wine from the German Rhineland
pop is British slang for pawn, to leave goods with a pawnbroker for a loan

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a Rhenish white wine; the other is slang for pawning an item, as in 'in hock'.

clue.text: Brave creatures being hunted

definitions.meaning: willing and spirited, ready to have a go
wild animals and birds pursued for sport

explanation.definitionFit: Plucky and willing as an adjective; quarry such as pheasant and deer as a noun.

clue.text: Trouble unfolded, alas, without warning

indicators.note: trouble as a verb means disturb, so these letters are stirred about

explanation.surface: A crisis suddenly erupted, sadly with no notice given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' looks like a noun but is the command to disturb UNFOLDED ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens abruptly arrives unexpectedly, with no advance notice.

clue.text: Pipe filled with a coin

indicators.note: filled with says the pipe holds the next letter inside

parts.note: a duct is a pipe or channel

explanation.surface: A coin is stuck inside a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold piece formerly used in several European countries.

clue.text: Rotor went wrong near Hyde Park corner

indicators.note: went wrong means these letters broke down into a new order

explanation.surface: A helicopter's blades failed close to a busy London junction.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyde Park Corner is a major London road junction; the riding track along the park's south side begins near it.
explanation.definitionFit: This sandy bridleway runs along the south side of Hyde Park from near the corner junction.

clue.text: Expert in car chases

indicators.note: in tells you the letters sit inside the words car chases, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A skilled driver at work in movie car chases.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means chief or pre-eminent, hence masterly and expert.

clue.text: To err is unusual — class going back to the beginning

indicators.note: is unusual says the letters of to err take an odd arrangement

parts.note: a grade is a class or rank

explanation.surface: Making mistakes is rare, yet the class is returning to square one.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrograde move reverts to an earlier, more primitive state.

clue.text: In this instance, it finally is put in the record and passed on

parts.note: here can mean in this case or instance

indicators.note: put in says a letter goes into the record word

parts.note: a diary is a daily written record

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of it

explanation.surface: In this case, an item is entered in the minutes and handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it finally' gives a single letter, and 'put in' slips it into the record word straight after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Traits or titles transmitted from parent to child descend through the generations.

clue.text: Scoffed after politician in pain produces snarl

indicators.note: after says the eating word follows the rest
in places the politician inside the word for pain

parts.note: colic is a sharp abdominal pain
MP, Member of Parliament, is the usual crossword politician
scoffed in the sense of gobbled up food means ate

explanation.surface: An MP in agony mocks and growls at people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' looks like mockery but means ate; 'snarl' is the verb to tangle, not a growl.
explanation.definitionFit: To snarl things is to tangle them, making matters more involved and difficult.

clue.text: Use spoon in jug

definitions.meaning: to mix a drink or sauce by moving a spoon round in it
jug is British slang for prison

explanation.definitionFit: Mixing with a spoon is the verb sense; prison is the slang noun, like the old word clink.

clue.text: Central office had concealed one point — and several others below

indicators.note: below, in a down entry, puts these letters after the rest
concealed says had hides the compass letter inside it

parts.note: taken as written
E, east, is one point of the compass
the quarters are the compass points or regions, so several other directions

explanation.surface: Head office kept one point secret, and others further down.
explanation.definitionFit: The base from which an organisation is directed is its main office.

clue.text: Unrepeatable offer Hector mistakenly derides at first

indicators.note: mistakenly says the letters of offer and Hector are set down in the wrong order
at first takes just the opening letter of derides

explanation.surface: Hector scornfully dismisses an offer that cannot be made again.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks given in confidence are not to be quoted or reported to others.

clue.text: The .country about to express disapproval at 25 Acts of Parliament

annotationWithheld.why: The country about to express disapproval at 25 Acts of Parliament (7,3): STATE around TUT gives STATUTE, but no reading of 'at 25' (25 is UPSIDE DOWN) gives LAW.
annotationWithheld.clue: The .country about to express disapproval at 25 Acts of Parliament

clue.text: The first to be stuck on a girl, a footballer — outside left

definitions.text: The first to be stuck on

parts.note: Penny is a girl's name

indicators.note: outside says the footballer goes round the left letter

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football

explanation.surface: A girl was the first to fall for a footballer playing outside left.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the world's first adhesive postage stamp, issued in Britain in 1840.
explanation.definitionFit: The first adhesive postage stamp, licked and stuck on letters from 1840.

clue.text: Financier, one restoring confidence heartlessly when at wit's end

indicators.note: when at places the final letter of wit before the trimmed word, at its head
the last letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the end of the word wit is its final letter

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the central letter, the ninth word's fifth letter

parts.note: someone who restores your confidence reassures you

explanation.surface: A banker comforts a client who is at their wits' end, but without real feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the central S of the restorer of confidence, a reassurer; 'end' picks the last letter of wit, set in front by 'when at'.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer who manages an organisation's funds is a money manager or financier.

clue.text: Privileged treatment brings communist rebuke

parts.note: a communist is called a red
to carpet someone is British slang for to reprimand them

explanation.surface: A Communist party member receives VIP handling then a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: To carpet someone is British slang for calling them in for a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: VIPs are welcomed by unrolling a crimson runner, so the phrase means special ceremonial welcome.

clue.text: Ventured to clean right inside.

indicators.note: inside says the right letter goes within the cleaning word

parts.note: to dust is to clean surfaces

explanation.surface: Someone dared to clean the inside of something properly.
explanation.definitionFit: An old past tense of dare, meaning plucked up courage to do something.

clue.text: Braced up to retreat from the rear

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: from the rear says the retreat word is read starting at its back

parts.note: a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: Soldiers steadied themselves to pull back away from the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscles that are firmed and strengthened are tightened, as in exercise.

clue.text: Where to find Victoria's sister in shabbier surroundings that I left

indicators.note: in places the sister inside what remains of the shabby word
that I left says the letter I departs from the shabby word

parts.note: dowdier means more drab and shabby
taken as written
a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: A woman's sister lives somewhere rather run-down, which the speaker has moved away from.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria here is the Australian state, not a woman; 'surroundings' frames the nun in DOWDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is a state of Australia, the country popularly called by this nickname.

clue.text: The. proper way to eat the food girl fed to old mistress

parts.note: table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

indicators.note: fed to says the girl goes into the mistress abbreviation

parts.note: Mrs began as the abbreviation of mistress, an older form of address
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's meal is served to an elderly lady of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' signals that the title Mrs began as short for mistress; 'fed to' puts the girl inside it to make the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette at meals, such as using cutlery correctly and not talking with a full mouth.

clue.text: Scots lad ups and joins the navy in Scots town

indicators.note: ups, in a down entry, says the name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Ian is a Scottish boy's name
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A Scottish boy signs up for the navy in his home town.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the Moray Firth in the Highlands of Scotland.

clue.text: One wet place? Just the opp-osite, a dry place

indicators.note: just the opposite says the letters for one wet place are turned round

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a bog is a marshy wet place

explanation.surface: Asked for somewhere wet, the speaker names the reverse: a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' turns I + BOG round end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast desert in Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: A love for indigo

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which is nil

explanation.surface: Someone's affection for a deep blue colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A West Indian shrub yielding a blue dye; the dye itself.

clue.text: Juvenile — 'e's in the chief part

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the boy

parts.note: a lad is a juvenile boy
the dropped-aitch 'e gives just the letter E

explanation.surface: Cockney boast: the youngster is starring in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e is Cockney he with the H dropped, so it gives only E.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal role in a play or film is the starring one.

clue.text: Form does wind up in total confusion

indicators.note: form, as a command, tells you to shape these letters into something new

explanation.surface: A form of bureaucracy that does tie someone in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like a noun but is the anagram command, applied to DOES WIND UP.
explanation.definitionFit: When everything is topsy-turvy it is in complete disorder or chaos.

clue.text: Having received approval, we became lively

indicators.note: having received says we takes the approval inside it

parts.note: taken as written
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Given the go-ahead, we perked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming out of sleep means rousing and becoming alert and active.

clue.text: Two saints getting sick come to a halt

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint, and there are two of them
getting is read as plus, which is and
the second of the two saint abbreviations
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Two holy men fall ill and must stop where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The two saints' STs are split by AND, which comes from 'getting' in the sense of plus.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete stop where nothing moves at all.
